archetype.name: Dual-Threat (designed-run)
archetype.definition: A second-year passer whose value rests on a quick, accurate short-to-intermediate game paired with called runs that move the chains, rather than on the deep ball or scrambling.

report.headline: One great game against a bad defense, then injured and buried at QB4
report.take:
Jaxson Dart's 2026 is effectively one game. In Week 1 against Dallas he went 23 of 29 for 230 yards and three touchdowns with 21.9 passing EPA, which accounts for almost all of his season. That game is why he leads all 45 qualifiers in EPA per dropback (0.578) and completion rate (76.5%). In Week 2 at the Rams he played 12% of the snaps, went 3 of 5 for 20 yards, and has not started since. Jameis Winston has started Weeks 3 through 6, Dart missed practice in Week 3, and as of October 20 the depth chart lists him as QB4. Treat any season-ranking you see for him with that in mind.

The Dallas game itself was real and fits who he is. The ball came out faster (2.64 seconds to throw against 2.82 last year), and the damage was done between the numbers and short of 20 yards. On intermediate throws he completed 72.7% for 1.167 EPA per attempt, and he went 8 of 9 on third down and 7 for 7 with three touchdowns in the red zone. He also ran 11 times for 54 yards, and the six designed runs averaged 8.17 a carry. That last part is the most reliable piece of his profile: last season he ranked 3rd of 63 in quarterback rushing yards.

The context cuts the other way. Dallas now ranks 31st in defensive EPA, so the season's highlight came against nearly the softest opponent available. The red-zone and third-down perfection rests on single-digit attempt counts, and those rates do not hold. His 2025 baseline is a more honest anchor: CPOE of -0.2 (35th of 63), a 15% bad-throw rate, and a pressure-to-sack rate that ranked 43rd of 62. Those are the habits of a raw passer. The 4.2-point CPOE jump is encouraging, but 34 attempts can't prove it is a new level. He also went 0 for 3 on throws of 20+ air yards.

The question now is availability and standing, not efficiency. Harbaugh's offense runs well below expectation (28th in pass rate over expected), and it has stuck with Winston for four weeks. Dart needs both health and a coaching decision to see the field again, and nothing in the dossier says either is imminent.

strengths.title: Designed-run game moves the chains
strengths.body: His called runs were the most efficient part of his short season: 1.056 EPA per play, every one a success, a third of them explosive. This is not a two-game fluke. He was 3rd among all quarterbacks in rushing yards as a rookie, so the legs are a durable part of his value. In a run-leaning Harbaugh offense, that gives him a role whenever he plays.

strengths.title: Accurate, on-time intermediate throws
strengths.body: Against Dallas he got the ball out faster than as a rookie and was sharp on throws of 10-19 air yards, the hardest zone for a young passer to own. Isaiah Likely was the main beneficiary, adding the most EPA of any target. The tool is real, but it was shown against a bottom-two defense on 11 attempts. It points toward growth rather than proving it.

concerns.title: Out of the lineup, fourth on depth chart
concerns.body: He left Week 2 after 12% of snaps, missed practice the following week, and Winston has started every game since. His site status reads Active, but the depth chart has him at QB4. That suggests the issue is now a standing problem with the coaches, not only an injury one. Until that changes, his ceiling is a clipboard.

concerns.title: Efficiency built on a soft opponent
concerns.body: Nearly all of his 20.8 passing EPA came in one game against a defense now ranked 31st. The perfect red-zone and near-perfect third-down lines sit on seven and nine attempts and will regress. His rookie accuracy and sack-avoidance numbers ranked in the bottom half, and this sample is too thin to overwrite them.

concerns.title: No vertical game yet
concerns.body: He went 0 of 3 on throws of 20+ air yards for -0.989 EPA each, and his intended air yards sit below the sticks on average. Three throws is a hint, not a verdict. Still, an offense that already passes little can't let defenses squat underneath if he returns.

trend.note: His season went from a 21.9-EPA opener to 12% of snaps in Week 2. He has not played since, with Winston starting four straight games and Dart sliding to QB4.

nextGame.headline: At Houston as a 10-point underdog, likely without Dart taking snaps
nextGame.body:
On paper, Houston's defense is one Dart's offense could attack. It allows 0.876 EPA on deep throws (27th) and the third-highest explosive pass rate, and it is a mild pass funnel. It also gets home (9th in sack rate), which is a problem for a quarterback whose rookie pressure-to-sack rate was among the worst. Shorter, quicker throws and designed runs would be his formula. Houston's run defense is above average (11th in rush EPA, 4th in explosive runs allowed), which limits that second piece.

Availability decides everything here, and it points away from him. He is QB4 behind Winston, so expect no meaningful role barring injuries ahead of him. Around the offense, right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor, a 90%-snap starter, is out. TE Theo Johnson is out, and WR Darnell Mooney is questionable with a neck injury. On Houston's side, safety Jalen Pitre is out and Reed Blankenship is questionable after a concussion. That thins the back end that has already been leaking big plays. The Book has the Giants as 10-point underdogs with a 42.5 total. The retractable roof and a mild early forecast keep weather out of it.

keyMatchups.title: Depth chart, not the defense
keyMatchups.body: Dart is listed fourth at quarterback and has not started since Week 2. Any snaps would likely come only through injury or a surprise benching of Winston. That makes his projection for this game close to zero, whatever the matchup looks like.

keyMatchups.title: Houston's leaky deep secondary
keyMatchups.body: Houston ranks near the bottom against deep throws and explosive passes, and it is missing Pitre with Blankenship in doubt. That is the area where Dart has shown the least this year. If he plays, it is a chance to show a vertical game he hasn't yet.

keyMatchups.title: Pass rush vs. thinned line
keyMatchups.body: Houston's sack rate ranks 9th, and the Giants lose their starting tackle Eluemunor. Paired with Dart's rookie tendency to take sacks under pressure, that makes this a bad setup for any quarterback dropped into this game cold.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Giants' weekly depth chart or practice reports move Dart back up behind or ahead of Winston. Nothing about him on the field matters until that happens.

restOfSeason.body:
The rest of the season hinges on a role he currently doesn't have. If he gets back into the lineup, expect a run-leaning offense to use him as a 20-to-30-attempt passer whose legs carry a steady share of his value. Expect efficiency well below the Week 1 peak: closer to his rookie EPA level than to a league-leading one, with the perfect red-zone and third-down rates falling to normal. The modest gains in accuracy and release time are worth tracking but unproven.

The projection ranges below run down to zero on purpose, because as QB4 his most likely weekly line is no line at all. The top of each range describes what a return to starting would look like: 150 to 210 passing yards, one or two total touchdowns, and 30 to 45 rushing yards. That is not the Dallas game repeated.
swingFactors: A return to the starting job over Winston
Whether the rookie sack and accuracy issues stay improved

confidence.note: Two games, one of them 12% of snaps. He is now QB4 with an unclear injury and role.
